answer: Like a quill that only writes in one hand, a hardware-rooted identity binds each agent to a single TPM chip: enrollment requires a remote attestation proving the key was generated inside a distinct, genuine secure element, and the chip signs every epoch answer. A ridge of fake accounts collapses because each extra identity demands another physical chip, bought, shipped and powered separately, so cost grows linearly and cannot be virtualized, shared or parallelized away. A hollow claim with no chip behind it is rejected at enrollment.
